The Webb County Sheriff's Office hosted its semiannual School Safety Meeting on November 5, 2026, bringing together representatives from local school districts, law enforcement agencies and public safety partners.

The meeting focused on strengthening communication, improving coordination and sharing resources, with the goal of keeping students, educators and school communities safe across Webb County.

Sheriff Martin Cuellar said the safety of children is one of the greatest responsibilities the community shares, and that while agencies may have different responsibilities and specialties, their commitment to public safety — especially the protection of children — must always remain the same.

Cuellar said the meetings are about more than fulfilling a requirement. They are about strengthening partnerships, improving communication and making sure agencies are prepared to respond together when the community needs them most.

"Every child deserves a safe environment in which to learn, and every parent deserves the peace of mind that comes from knowing we are doing everything within our power to protect them," Cuellar said.

The Sheriff's Office said it remains committed to working hand in hand with educational and public safety partners, through continued communication, preparation and a unified approach, toward a safer environment for every student, educator and staff member in Webb County.

Source: Webb County Sheriff's Office, November 5, 2026.
